intended_object: The barycentric coordinate vector of the vertex `c` in the geometric realization of the Fox–Neuwirth order complex: the function on `BarredPermutation p` that is 1 at `c` and 0 elsewhere (the standard basis vector e_c). This comes from the docstring and from its only use, building `vertex`.
explanation: The body is `fun d => if d = c then 1 else 0`, which is exactly the indicator vector e_c = `Pi.single c 1`. It is correct for what it is meant to be. It is a small helper whose only job is to supply the underlying function of the subtype element `Realization.vertex c`, the realization point that is the vertex c. The three proof obligations proved right after it are nonnegativity, summing to one and chain support. It is an implementation step for building `vertex`, not a mathematical notion the library introduces in its own right. The underlying idea, the standard basis vector, already exists in Mathlib as `Pi.single c 1`, and the definition agrees with it pointwise. Fixing the codomain to ℝ and the index type to `BarredPermutation p` is forced by the `Realization p` structure it feeds into, so this is not a case of undue narrowness either way. The only real candidate verdict is `faithful`. Since it is auxiliary data for constructing `vertex`, I classify it as `not_a_mathematical_object`.
